2187: Bus i takes time[i] units per trip and repeats trips immediately; buses operate independently from time zero. Return the minimum elapsed time for all buses together to complete at least totalTrips trips.
2220: One operation flips any one bit. Return the minimum bit flips needed to convert start to goal.
2225: Each match lists a winner and loser. Return two sorted lists of players who participated: those with no losses, and those with exactly one loss.
2226: Split candy piles into smaller piles, without merging. Give k children equal positive integer amounts, with each child's share taken from one resulting pile. Candies may remain unused. Return the largest amount per child, or 0.
2300: For each spell, count potions whose strength times that spell's strength is at least success. Return counts in spell order; potions are reusable across separate spell queries.
2305: Distribute whole cookie bags among k children. A child's total is the sum of assigned bags; unfairness is the largest child's total. Return the minimum possible unfairness.
2335: Each second fill either two cups of different types or one cup of any type. Return the minimum seconds needed to fill the three required type counts.
2353: Implement FoodRatings(foods,cuisines,ratings), changeRating(food,newRating), and highestRated(cuisine). Return the food with the greatest current rating in that cuisine, breaking ties lexicographically. Food names/cuisines do not change.
2368: In an undirected tree rooted at 0, restricted vertices cannot be visited. Return how many vertices, including 0, are reachable without entering a restricted vertex; 0 is not restricted.
2402: Assign each half-open meeting [start,end) to the lowest-numbered available room. If all rooms are busy, delay it until a room frees, preserving duration and priority by original start time. Count meetings per room; return the most-used room, breaking ties by smallest number.
2410: Match players to trainers when trainer capacity is at least player ability. Each participant is used at most once. Return the maximum number of matches.
2462: Hire exactly k workers sequentially. Each round considers the first candidates and last candidates remaining workers; choose minimum cost, breaking ties by original index. Overlapping windows count workers once. Remove the chosen worker and return total cost.
2491: Pair all players so every team's skill sum is equal. Team chemistry is the product of its players' skills. Return total chemistry, or -1 if no valid pairing exists.
2542: Choose k indices. Their score is the sum of nums1 at those indices multiplied by the minimum nums2 value at the same indices. Return the maximum score.
2558: Exactly k times, choose a pile with the most gifts and leave floor(sqrt(pile)) gifts there. Return the number of gifts remaining across all piles.
2578: Distribute all decimal digits of num between two integers, allowing leading zeros and arbitrary digit order. Return their smallest possible sum.
2587: Reorder nums to maximize the number of strictly positive prefix sums. Return that maximum count; each input occurrence must be used exactly once.
2597: Count nonempty index subsets containing no two values with absolute difference k. Equal values at different indices represent separate choices.
2616: Choose p disjoint index pairs to minimize the largest absolute difference within any chosen pair. Return that minimum, or 0 if p=0.
2642: Implement Graph(n,edges) for a directed weighted graph: addEdge(edge) adds a directed edge, and shortestPath(node1,node2) returns the minimum path cost or -1 if unreachable. Paths from a node to itself have cost 0.
3066: Repeatedly remove the two smallest values x<=y and insert 2*x+y. Return the minimum operations until every value is at least k. The input guarantees this is possible.
3075: Select exactly k children sequentially. Each selection adds that child's current happiness, then decreases every unselected child's happiness by 1, never below 0. Return the maximum total happiness.
